entry.summary: 2 minute read Sony RIALTO 65: specs, price, and release date 3:06 Sony's just confirmed RIALTO 65 Camera Extension System expands the VENICE 2 to 65mm and is due in the first half of 2027 for $80,000. Sony's newly confirmed RIALTO 65 Camera Extension System for the VENICE 2 CineA
entry.content:
2 minute read
Sony RIALTO 65: specs, price, and release date
3:06

Sony's just confirmed RIALTO 65 Camera Extension System expands the VENICE 2 to 65mm and is due in the first half of 2027 for $80,000.

Sony's newly confirmed RIALTO 65 Camera Extension System for the VENICE 2 CineAlta camera expands VENICE 2 to the 65mm format. First announced back in June at Cine Gear Expo the CBK-6510XS is due in the first half of 2027.

The sensor measures 53.75 mm (2.12 in) wide by 35.83 mm (1.41 in) high, with a diagonal of approximately 64.60 mm (2.54 in). Sony reckons it is among the largest image sensors used in commercially available cinema cameras, with an imaging area approximately 2.2 times larger than a 35mm full-frame sensor.

Studio Mode, Extension Mode, and cable options

The camera head measures approximately 115 mm x 154 mm x 63 mm (4.5 in x 6.1 in x 2.5 in) and weighs approximately 1.5 kg (3.3 lb). In Extension Mode the head can be separated from the VENICE 2 body, while in Studio Mode it is attached directly to the body. The connecting cable detaches at both ends. A 4.5 m (14.8 ft) cable is included, and a 12 m (39.4 ft) cable will be available.

It supports 9.6K 1.5:1 Open Gate readout and a 9.6K 2.20:1 readout mode with a diagonal of approximately 59.04 mm (2.32 in). Additional readout modes will arrive through future software updates to the VENICE 2 body. Base ISO is 2500 or 10000, with 15+ stops of latitude at ISO 2500.

The VENICE 2 body handles recording, including internal 16-bit X-OCN, on AXS memory cards. S-Log3 and S-Gamut3 are carried over.

Here are the imager modes and current caveats.

Lenses, anamorphic support, and ND filters

RIALTO 65 has no lens mount of its own and accepts third-party lens-mount adapters, including those for 65mm-format lenses. With a lens and adapter that communicate with the camera, focal length, focus position, and aperture value are recorded as metadata. Anamorphic shooting is supported with de-squeeze display at multiple magnification ratios and a Zoom to Fit function. Camera tilt and roll are recorded as metadata.

Eleven drop-in ND filters with electronic contacts are included, and VENICE 2 automatically recognizes the density of an inserted filter. The CBK-NDK6510 ND Filter Kit is a set of 11 drop-in ND filters equivalent to those included, and individual filters cannot be purchased separately.

Pricing

Sony has set a US MSRP of $80,000 (C$113,800 in Canada) for the RIALTO 65, with availability tentatively in the first half of 2027. The CBK-NDK6510 ND Filter Kit is $8,000 (C$11,380), and the optional 12 m (39.4 ft) CBK-12C6510 cable is $9,000 (C$12,800). Additionally, VENICE 2 bodies will need dedicated firmware, version 6.00 or later. Sony cautions that specifications are current as of the announcement date and may differ from the final ones.

entry.title: SmallHD Focus 504: specs, price and PageOS
entry.summary: 1 minute read SmallHD Focus 504: specs, price and PageOS 1:49 The 5-in Focus 504 is SmallHD's thinnest monitor yet at a mere 20 mm (0.8 in). It offers up to 1000 nits and PageOS for $999. SmallHD has launched the Focus 504 monitor, an addition to its expanding range of on-camera
entry.content:
1 minute read
SmallHD Focus 504: specs, price and PageOS
1:49

The 5-in Focus 504 is SmallHD's thinnest monitor yet at a mere 20 mm (0.8 in). It offers up to 1000 nits and PageOS for $999.

SmallHD has launched the Focus 504 monitor, an addition to its expanding range of on-camera monitors featuring a low-profile form factor and die-cast aluminum construction. It ships with the built-in PageOS Monitoring Toolkit with optional future licenses for camera control.

The Focus 504 is SmallHD’s thinnest monitor to date, at 136 x 88 x 20 mm (5.4 x 3.5 x 0.8 in). It weighs 306.25 g (0.68 lb).

The 5 in edge-lit display is 1920 x 1080, with up to 1000 nits brightness and 100% Rec. 709 coverage, with 10-bit processing (though the panel itself is 8-bit). I/O is extensive at 1x 3G-SDI in, 1x 3G-SDI out, 1x HDMI 2.0 in, 1x HDMI 2.0 out, 1x locking USB-C for PVC (Power / Video / Communication), and 2x locking USB-C (5V / 1.5A).

Power input is via a 2-pin locking connector or locking USB-C PVC. Internal 2.4 GHz WiFi allows for cable-less camera control with the appropriate license. The aluminum chassis has four integrated 1/4"-20 (ARRI Locking Pin) mounting points.

PageOS is navigated by touchscreen and/or the joystick along with two function/menu buttons on the back of the panel. Tools include Portrait Mode, Waveform, Vectorscope, EL Zone, False Color, and LUT workflows, and the UI rotates when shooting vertical.

Pricing and availability

The SmallHD Focus 504 costs $999 and is available immediately. Add-on licenses, sold separately is coming soon and will cover camera control over ARRI, RED, Canon, and Sony cameras.

entry.title: Accsoon CineView Master 4K II: specs and price
entry.summary: 2 minute read Accsoon CineView Master 4K II: specs and price 3:09 Accsoon's flagship tri-band wireless system gains a camera-control port and a receiver USB-C output. The CineView Master 4K II costs $899. Accsoon has announced the CineView Master 4K II, the second generation of i
entry.content:
2 minute read
Accsoon CineView Master 4K II: specs and price
3:09

Accsoon's flagship tri-band wireless system gains a camera-control port and a receiver USB-C output. The CineView Master 4K II costs $899.

Accsoon has announced the CineView Master 4K II, the second generation of its flagship tri-band wireless video system. The big additions are camera control from a phone or tablet and a USB-C video output on the receiver.

Neither feature is new to the CineView range. Accsoon added camera control and USB-C video output at both ends to the CineView SE 4K, which we covered in March, and to the CineView Master 4K Lite in April. The Master 4K II finally brings them to the top model.

Camera control

The transmitter has a dedicated USB-C camera-control port. With a supported camera connected, the Accsoon SEE app on a phone or tablet can start and stop recording, set touch focus, and adjust ISO, aperture, white balance, and shutter speed. Supported cameras are the Sony FX3, FX30, A7C II, A7S III, A7 IV, and A9 III, and the Canon R5, R6, R5 II, R6 II, R7, and R8. Accsoon says it plans to add support for other makers, as well as more Canon and Sony models.

There is one caveat to be aware of. Camera control works only when the mobile device connects to the transmitter over WiFi, and it is unavailable through the receiver's USB connection.

USB-C at both ends

The original Master 4K offered a USB-C video output on the transmitter only. The II adds one to the receiver, so a phone or tablet can be cabled in at the camera and at the monitoring position. Connected devices charge while monitoring, and up to 10 devices can watch the feed at once.

The transmission side carries over from the previous model. The system uses the 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz bands simultaneously, with Accsoon's proprietary RTMS 4.0 protocol. But one significant upgrade is that the II transmits DCI 4K and UHD at up to 60 fps with H.265 encoding, where the original handled UHD only.

Accsoon quotes ideal-scenario latency under 25 ms at 1080p60 and under 35 ms at 4K60 (excluding camera latency) and a range of 2.5 km (1.55 miles).

Connections and power

The transmitter takes HDMI 2.0 and 3G SDI input, with an HDMI 2.0 loop-out. The receiver outputs HDMI 2.0 and 3G SDI. Power comes from NP-F batteries or 12 V DC input, with Accsoon V-mount and Gold-mount adapters sold separately.

Each unit measures 130 × 95 × 32 mm (5.1 × 3.7 × 1.3 in) without antennas. The transmitter weighs 322 g (11.4 oz) and the receiver 320 g (11.3 oz). The system supports Frame.io Camera to Cloud through a compatible mobile workflow, and it works with the CineView Master 4K, Master 4K Lite, SE 4K, M7 Pro, and M7H Pro.

Price and availability

The CineView Master 4K II kit costs $899, slightly up from the original’s $849 launch price, and pre-orders are open now.

entry.summary: 1 minute read Nikon Z 120-300mm f/2.8 TC VR S: specs, price 2:43 Nikon’s new sports zoom pairs a constant f/2.8 aperture with a built-in 1.4x teleconverter. It weighs 2735 g (6.03 lb) and costs a whopping $13,999 from November. Nikon has unveiled the NIKKOR Z 120-300mm f/2.8 TC V
entry.content:
1 minute read
Nikon Z 120-300mm f/2.8 TC VR S: specs, price
2:43

Nikon’s new sports zoom pairs a constant f/2.8 aperture with a built-in 1.4x teleconverter. It weighs 2735 g (6.03 lb) and costs a whopping $13,999 from November.

Nikon has unveiled the NIKKOR Z 120-300mm f/2.8 TC VR S, which it says is the world’s first telephoto zoom lens with a constant f/2.8 aperture and built-in 1.4x teleconverter.

Designed for professional sports photographers, Nikon first announced development of the lens back in May, when we assumed it would be north of $10,000. And at $13,999, we certainly got that part right.

It’s a beast. The built-in teleconverter extends the focal-length range from 120-300mm to 168-420mm, while photographers can go to 630mm in DX crop mode. Optics include Super ED and SR glass, with Meso Amorphous and ARNEO coatings. The built-in teleconverter reaches 420mm at f/4, and Nikon says image quality is comparable to that of a prime lens with the teleconverter engaged.

In-lens Vibration Reduction is rated at up to 6.5 stops. AF uses a multi-focus system with Silky Swift voice coil motors and what Nikon says is a new control algorithm that should keep pace with the fastest continuous shooting speeds whatever you’re throwing at it.

Significantly lighter

The lens is lighter than before, weighing approximately 2735 g (6.03 lb), about 515 g (1.14 lb) less than its F-mount predecessor, even with the built-in teleconverter. At 353.5 mm (13.9 in), Nikon says it will fit into international-standard carry-on bags, which is good as it would be a brave person that sticks a lens like this in the hold. The internal zoom keeps the center of gravity consistent, which is useful when corralling something with that amount of heft.

The control ring can also be used as a focus ring, and functions can be assigned to two L-Fn buttons or the Fn ring. Sealing protects against dust, dirt, and moisture, though Nikon says the lens is not guaranteed to be dust- and drip-resistant in all situations and conditions. The front element has a fluorine coat.

The tripod collar is Arca-Swiss compatible with screw-type clamps; lever-type clamps may not provide sufficient holding strength and are not recommended. Front screw-in and rear drop-in filters are supported.

Pricing and availability

The NIKKOR Z 120-300mm f/2.8 TC VR S costs $13,999, with sales starting in November 2026.

entry.title: MacBook Pro PROLED XDR: price and release date
entry.summary: 2 minute read MacBook Pro PROLED XDR: price and release date 4:46 Apple's MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is a tandem OLED laptop with Touch, available to pre-order today from $2899. It ships November 6. Drumroll please. Apple has introduced the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Di
entry.content:
2 minute read
MacBook Pro PROLED XDR: price and release date
4:46

Apple's MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is a tandem OLED laptop with Touch, available to pre-order today from $2899. It ships November 6.

Drumroll please. Apple has introduced the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, a tandem OLED panel in 14- and 16-inch models. And if you thought previous Macs were expensive, it’s time to recalibrate your opinions. These machines start at $2899, $700 more than their non-touchscreen screen forefathers.

But, despite the company being famously resistant to the concept, these are finally the first Mac with Touch. The sensor is built into the display panel, and macOS translates touches into clicks, with the idea being many existing apps work with it immediately. Updated system gesture APIs are available to developers, and Apple lists Adobe Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, Blender, Maxon Cinema 4D, Maxon ZBrush, Shapr3D, Algoriddim djay Pro, Notion, Canva, Zoom, and Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook as apps that will support Touch later this year. For now, Pixelmator Pro, Logic Pro, and Final Cut Pro in Apple Creator Studio are already optimized for it with their new versions dropping next month.

The Dynamic Island also finally arrives on Mac as the home for Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI.

For those looking nervously at the iPhone Duo “crackgate” problems, Apple says a redesigned hinge improves stability, and video stabilization smooths the camera feed on video calls while Touch is in use.

Screen specs

As you would expect, the screen is top of the range. It offers up to 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness, a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio, and ProMotion refresh rates from 10 Hz to 120 Hz. It covers P3 and Adobe RGB, with more than 80% Rec. 2020 coverage, and both color spaces sit in a single default preset. Each panel is factory calibrated. The display engine controls color and luminance of every pixel at the sub-millisecond level, compensating for content, pixel use, temperature, and environment, and adapts each pixel’s usage over time. An antireflective coating is standard, and the nano-texture option is now etched into the cover glass.

This has plenty of pro-level tools to ensure color-critical workflows proceed as planned. The Apple Pro Display Calibrator and industry-standard reference modes are included, along with DICOM modes for nondiagnostic review, research, and education. Apple says its Color Matching Function 2026 aligns the display with iPhone 18 Pro and Studio Display XDR. Genlock support synchronizes the display refresh rate with camera capture, enabled by compatible third-party hardware and software.

Thinner and lighter

In terms of physical dimensions, the 14-inch model weighs 1.4 kg (3 lb), 0.2 kg (0.5 lb) less than before, and is 0.5 mm (0.02 in) thinner. The 16-inch weighs 1.8 kg (4 lb), 0.3 kg (0.7 lb) less, and is nearly 1 mm (0.04 in) thinner. Battery life is up to 24 hours, and fast charge reaches 50% in 30 minutes.

The new machines are based on the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, already making them effectively a generation behind yesterday’s latest announced M6 MacBooks. They’re no slouches though. M5 Pro and M5 Max support up to 128 GB of unified memory, and storage is configurable up to 16 TB. Each GPU core has a Neural Accelerator, and the GPU has enhanced shader cores, a third-generation ray-tracing engine, and Dynamic Caching. M5 Max can run LLMs with hundreds of billions of parameters on device.

The six-speaker system has a new woofer for 50% deeper bass and supports Spatial Audio with Dolby Atmos. Audio is tuned for closed-lid use with an external display.

Connectivity is as you would expect for such a pro-targeted machine, and is covered with three Thunderbolt 5 ports, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe, and a headphone jack. M5 Pro supports up to three external displays and M5 Max up to four, which will be something to see. WiFi 7, Bluetooth 6, Touch ID, and a 12 MP Center Stage camera are included.

Pricing and availability

Hold onto your hats. US pricing starts at $2899 for the 14-inch with M5 Pro, $3399 for the 16-inch with M5 Pro, $4499 for the 14-inch with M5 Max, and $4799 for the 16-inch with M5 Max. Pre-orders open today, October 28, in 30 countries and regions, with availability from Friday, November 6.

entry.title: Sony FX5 delay: Europe now lists January 8
entry.summary: 1 minute read Sony FX5 delay: Europe now lists January 8 1:26 Sony's FX5 cinema camera has slipped again in Europe at least , with multiple Sony sites in now listing its shipping date as January 8. We were really hoping not to have to use this graphic again. But, while all the mo
entry.content:
1 minute read
Sony FX5 delay: Europe now lists January 8
1:26

Sony's FX5 cinema camera has slipped again in Europe at least , with multiple Sony sites in now listing its shipping date as January 8.

We were really hoping not to have to use this graphic again. But, while all the mood music from out of the US is that the long-awaited Sony FX5 will actually ship in early to mid-November, Sony's own direct-to-consumer sites in multiple European countries paint a bleaker picture. Sites including those in the UK, France, and Germany now list January 8 as the first ship date for pre-orders, nearly two months later than their previous listing.

A new statement from Sony Japan, the first since September on the subject, lists availability as November 20. US listings at resellers such as Adorama say that pre-orders are open now and that the expected availability starts at November 16.

As before, the postponement (or lack of postponement, depending on where you are) covers the FX5 camera body along with three related accessories: the DVF-EL1 OLED viewfinder, the XLR-H2 XLR handle unit, and the VMC-BNCU1 timecode adapter cable.

What's going on? To be honest, it's difficult to know. Sony has played its cards very close to its chest ever since the first delays back in August, but it looks like the initial problems were with the rear LCD, as PetaPixel reported. As far as anyone was aware, those had been fixed and the cameras were on their way to retailers.

An optimistic reading is that Sony is swamped by order volume, that the stock simply isn’t there to fill new European orders, and that existing orders will still ship in mid-November. A more pessimistic one points to the lack of an official US ship date and wonders whether Sony’s European sites are the canary in the coal mine for delays elsewhere as they have been before. We're just crossing our fingers and hoping at this point...

entry.summary: 1 minute read amaran Cam: 4K60 webcam with Auto Lighting, $249 2:20 The amaran Cam captures 4K60 and adjusts connected amaran lights to match what it sees. It costs $249 and is available now. amaran has announced the amaran Cam, its first webcam, and earns itself an over-achiever
entry.content:
1 minute read
amaran Cam: 4K60 webcam with Auto Lighting, $249
2:20

The amaran Cam captures 4K60 and adjusts connected amaran lights to match what it sees. It costs $249 and is available now.

amaran has announced the amaran Cam, its first webcam, and earns itself an over-achiever award by integrating a novel Auto Lighting feature into it as well.

The camera captures 4K60 with a 1/1.3" sensor and an f/1.68 aperture. It has all the features you would expect: 2× lossless zoom while maintaining full 4K resolution, and autofocus that locks onto subjects in under 1/4 second with reduced focus hunting. Up to four amaran Cams can be connected, with quick switching between views. Rotating the webcam switches to native 9:16 output at up to 4K60, without cropping, and it is tuned to a range of different skin tones.

Auto Lighting

The Auto Lighting feature is where the differentiation is, and as far as we know it’s a first. It analyzes the exposure on the creator’s face through the amaran Desktop App and adjusts connected amaran lights, reaching what the company says is a camera-ready result in 10 seconds.

amaran started with lighting, and at launch Auto Lighting supports up to two compatible amaran lights, with plans to expand support to more complex multi-light setups through future software updates. For two-light setups there are three looks: Even for clean, balanced lighting; Defined for added shape and depth; or Bold for stronger contrast and mood.

The amaran Desktop App provides centralized control over camera settings and connected amaran lighting and audio, plus Green Screen, Beauty, and Filters in Virtual Camera mode. Active cooling supports at least 72 hours of continuous operation at 4K60.

It works with all the usual suspects such as OBS Studio, Streamlabs, Twitch, Zoom, Teams, and more. Size is 7.39 x 3.78 x 3.28 cm (2.91 x 1.49 x 1.29 in), and the camera weighs 69 g (0.15 lb).

Pricing and availability

The amaran Cam costs $249 and is available now. A streaming bundle with amaran Verge lighting and the amaran Mic is also available starting at $415 (one light and stand) and $545 (two lights and stands).

entry.title: Apple Creator Studio update: MotionVFX and AI
entry.summary: 3 minute read Apple Creator Studio update: MotionVFX and AI 5:36 Apple Creator Studio's November update, free to existing subscribers, puts MotionVFX inside Final Cut Pro. Logic Pro, Keynote, Pages, and Numbers gain beta AI assistants. While everyone was primed for Apple hardware
entry.content:
3 minute read
Apple Creator Studio update: MotionVFX and AI
5:36

Apple Creator Studio's November update, free to existing subscribers, puts MotionVFX inside Final Cut Pro. Logic Pro, Keynote, Pages, and Numbers gain beta AI assistants.

While everyone was primed for Apple hardware releases today, much more unexpected was a new version of Apple Creator Studio for Mac, iPad, and iPhone. Apple’s creative apps used to be updated with fairly glacial slowness, but Apple seems to have kicked things up a gear now that it has Creator Studio subscriptions to sell. Creator Studio only went on sale in January this year, and this will be the fourth update to hit the App Store.

Final Cut Pro gets supercharged

Final Cut Pro for Mac probably gets the biggest update across the range, and now includes built-in MotionVFX, following Apple’s purchase of the company back in March. This adds thousands of elements, including effects, plug-ins, transitions, templates, titles, graphics, and tools for rotoscoping, tracking, and color grading. Also, any image on the timeline can now be opened in Pixelmator Pro and saved back to the project automatically.

Apple is less front and center with AI tools than some rivals, but all the same, Final Cut Pro adds AI image generation from text descriptions. Elsewhere it gets more keyframe easing options, the ability to disconnect clips from the primary storyline and place them anywhere on the timeline, and 23 new transcription languages.

The Content Hub, an Apple-curated library of stock videos, photos, and backgrounds, now includes video assets and is available in Final Cut Pro. No word yet on its size, but it’s interesting to see Cupertino expand on what it contains.

Motion and Pixelmator Pro

In the wider app portfolio, Motion adds built-in MotionVFX plug-ins for color grading, 3D camera tracking, and one-click selection, plus image generation from text descriptions, round-tripping to Pixelmator Pro, keyframe easing, a Displacement filter, and an interactive demo project. Compressor can encode Cinematic mode video recorded on iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo.

Pixelmator Pro itself unsurprisingly adds Generate Fill, which realistically sees it playing catch-up with rival image editing software. This edits a user-selected area from a text description, matching lighting, perspective, and the texture of the surrounding area. Built-in Super Resolution upscales the generated content. Generated elements can be merged into existing layers or inserted as new layers with masking.

Logic Pro updates

Logic Pro for Mac and iPad gets a Liquid Glass design, while Logic Pro for Mac adds an assistant in beta, powered by Apple-built models and OpenAI, for navigating production workflows, starting a song, setting up a vocal track from a single prompt, or refining a project. It also gets a redesigned Browser covering loops, instruments, effect patches, and a Splice library.

Music understanding, an on-device audio analysis tool, classifies and tags added sounds, so users can search the whole collection or drag in a loop to find matching audio, which should save time wading through libraries of sounds. Stem Splitter can also now isolate, replace, or rebalance drum parts without the original multitracks. A new Producer Pack from Sergio George includes his piano sound and Latin jazz and salsa loops, including percussion, brass, and basses. Voice Memo Studio Sound reduces room ambience and background noise in recordings from supported iPhone models, with the option to continue in Logic Pro.

Productivity? Sweet...

And the more controversial members of the Creator Studio offering, the everyday productivity apps of Keynote, Pages, and Numbers, also get new features. This starts with an assistant in beta, built on Apple models and OpenAI, that understands document context. In Keynote it helps design, animate, and refine slides; in Pages it drafts, restructures, and fine-tunes text; and in Numbers it calculates, visualizes, and organizes data, recommends chart types with a one-tap preview, and builds custom tables using world knowledge.

Model Context Protocol (MCP) support lets external AI agents and tools read content, perform edits, and run automated actions. The Content Hub in Keynote, Pages, and Numbers adds stock video, and there are new templates and themes. Keynote adds support for Keynote Interchange Format (.keyx), an open JSON-based bundle format. Freeform adds text styles for formatting and reuse across boards, plus custom and preset board background colors. In December it will add image editing in Pixelmator Pro and generation of editable shapes from text.

Pricing and availability

The update arrives on the App Store in November, free for existing subscribers. In the US, new subscribers pay $12.99 per month or $129 per year, with a one-month free trial. Customers who buy a new Mac or qualifying iPad can receive three months free. Education pricing for college students and educators is $2.99 per month or $29.99 per year. Creator Studio is a universal purchase, and up to six family members can share it with Family Sharing. One-time purchases on the Mac App Store are Final Cut Pro ($299), Logic Pro ($199), Pixelmator Pro ($49.99), Motion ($49.99), Compressor ($49.99), and MainStage ($29.99). Free versions of Keynote, Pages, Numbers, and Freeform remain available and come with every new iPhone, Mac, and iPad.

entry.title: M6 iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro: specs and prices
entry.summary: 2 minute read M6 iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro: specs and prices 4:34 Apple has announced two new computers, the 24-inch iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro, both built around the M6 chip. Prices start from $1499 and $1999. And still we wait for tomorrow and the official announcement of
entry.content:
2 minute read
M6 iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro: specs and prices
4:34

Apple has announced two new computers, the 24-inch iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro, both built around the M6 chip. Prices start from $1499 and $1999. And still we wait for tomorrow and the official announcement of the touchscreen MacBooks.

24-inch M6 iMac

We’ll start with the new 24-inch iMac with M6. It comes with a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU, or up to a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, each two more cores than before. The GPU has Neural Accelerators in each core, and there is a Dual 16-core Neural Engine. Memory bandwidth is up to 170 GB/s.

Apple loves its benchmarks and says that the GPU delivers up to 2x faster graphics than M4, the Neural Engine up to 2x faster AI compute than the previous generation, on-device AI up to 5x faster than M4, and SSD read and write up to 2x faster.

For Intel-based upgraders (if there are any left out there), Apple quotes up to 18x faster performance than the most popular Intel-based iMac.

The 4.5K Retina display has an actual diagonal of 23.5 inches, 500 nits of brightness, and P3 wide color covering over 1 billion colors. Apple says it has 5x more resolution and nearly 70% greater brightness than the bestselling 24-inch all-in-one PC, but that’s enough of a limited category it doesn’t feel like a particularly valid comparison. A nano-texture option is available on the more expensive 12-core models.

Connectivity is WiFi 7 and Bluetooth 6, with optional 2.5 Gb Ethernet (up to 2.5x faster wired than the previous generation) and up to four Thunderbolt 4 ports on 12-core models. It supports up to two 6K external displays. There is a 12 MP Center Stage camera with Desk View, two pairs of force-cancelling woofers with two tweeters, Spatial Audio with Dolby Atmos support, and a three-microphone array.

The iMac comes in seven colors: blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange, and silver. It includes a color-matched keyboard and mouse or trackpad with USB-C ports. Touch ID is standard on 12-core models, while 10-core models can be configured with Magic Keyboard with Touch ID and Numeric Keypad.

Pricing and availability

Pre-orders open October 28 in 35 countries and regions, with availability from Friday, November 6. The 10-core model starts at $1499. The 12-core model starts at $1699. Apple Upgrade leasing starts at $28.99 per month for 36 months, excluding taxes and trade-in credit.

14-inch MacBook Pro with M6

The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 also raises the bar over its predecessors to an impressive degree. The chip has a 12-core CPU, a 12-core GPU with a Neural Accelerator in each core, and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine; the CPU and GPU each have two more cores than before. Memory is 16 GB unified as standard, configurable up to 32 GB, with bandwidth up to 170 GB/s. Apple says the GPU is up to 30% faster for graphics and up to 25% faster for AI workloads than M5, and that the Neural Engine is up to 1.9x faster than M5.

One more benchmark comparison is well worth noting: battery life is up to 24 hours, which is up to 14 hours more for Intel-based upgraders and up to four hours more for M1 users. It’s also the same as with the M5 model.

The Liquid Retina XDR display reaches up to 1600 nits peak HDR brightness with a 1,000,000:1 contrast ratio, and a nano-texture option is available. Connectivity includes WiFi 7, Bluetooth 6, support for up to two external displays, HDMI, MagSafe 3, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, an SDXC card slot, and a headphone jack.

There is also a 12 MP Center Stage camera with Desk View, a three-mic array, and a six-speaker system with Spatial Audio.

Fast charging reaches up to 50% in 30 minutes with a compatible higher-wattage USB-C adapter such as the 96 W Power Adapter.

Pricing and availability

It comes in space black and silver. Pre-orders open October 28 in 35 countries and regions, with availability from Friday, November 6. Pricing starts at $1999. Apple Upgrade leasing starts at $38.99 per month for 36 months, excluding taxes and trade-in credit.

entry.content:
2 minute read
DaVinci Resolve 21.1.2: new features and fixes
3:07

Blackmagic has improved timeline edit point selection and made OGraf playback up to 4x faster in DaVinci Resolve 21.1.2. Studio also speeds up IntelliSearch on Apple M6.

Blackmagic has released DaVinci Resolve 21.1.2 and Fusion Studio 21.1.2, following the major 21.1 release in September and 21.1.1 earlier this month.

DaVinci Resolve 21.1.2 adds improved timeline edit point selection, as well as up to 4x faster OGraf playback, additional template controls, and support for OGraf and Lottie graphics on Linux. The OGraf changes are also in Fusion Studio 21.1.2, which adds custom clip input and output labels for OpenFX.

DaVinci Resolve Studio 21.1.2 adds IntelliSearch analysis that Blackmagic says is up to 14x faster on Apple M6 computers running macOS 27.IntelliSearch analysis, multicam SmartSwitch, and other AI tools run faster on Intel graphics platforms, while Magic Mask caches use less disk space, and there are multiple scripting API improvements. The software is currently 20% off until November 20.

As usual, all updates are free and available from the Blackmagic support page. Here are the full changelogs of new or updated features.

What's new in DaVinci Resolve 21.1.2

The following features have been added or updated.

  • Select nearest edit point type prioritizes selected edit points.
  • Lasso selecting edit points can now enter dynamic trim automatically.
  • Selecting edit points for gaps now activates trim editor.
  • Timeline view option to display current clip indicator.
  • Option to show loudness meters in the edit mixer.
  • Project settings option to disable DNG lens correction.
  • OGraf clips now use action durations to place stop actions.
  • Up to 4x faster OGraf playback in edit and Fusion pages.
  • Support for OGraf select and multi-select template controls.
  • OGraf responsive templates now adapt to timeline aspect ratio.
  • Support for OGraf and Lottie graphics on Linux.
  • Improved HDR global wheel trackball sensitivity on color panels.
  • Fast Noise option to follow the FX tracker.
  • Addressed double squeezed anamorphic video output in Fusion.
  • Addressed issue with Follower animation using expressions.
  • Addressed overlay issues with SDI and remote monitoring.
  • Addressed issue with searches in a smart bin.
  • Addressed empty folder in user directory when loading DRP files.
  • Addressed issue with selecting multiple titles and subtitles.
  • Addressed timeline in-out range issues in collaboration projects.
  • Addressed Quick Export not using selected trim pass grade.
  • Addressed issue with geometry thumbnails in the media pool.
  • Addressed Recent 5 Mins mode inserting full clips.
  • Addressed loudness meter not resetting after Cut page scrubbing.
  • General performance and stability improvements.

In addition to the above, Resolve Studio 21.1.2 adds the following:

  • Up to 14x faster IntelliSearch analysis on M6 with macOS 27.
  • Improved AI tool performance on Intel platforms.
  • Improved disk space usage for Magic Mask caches.
  • Multiple scripting API improvements.
  • Addressed issue with Film Look Creator gate weave controls.
  • Addressed HDR Vivid metadata issues in imported CPL timelines.
  • Addressed Speech Generator disk usage and speed on macOS 27.
  • Addressed issues with Music Remixer on macOS 27.
  • Addressed render failures for in-out ranges with Magic Mask clips.
  • General performance and stability improvements.

What's new in Fusion Studio 21.1.2

The following features have been added or updated.

  • Addressed issue with channel names in Displace 3D.
  • Addressed issue with running some Lua scripts.
  • Addressed memory issue with some Perspective Positioner settings.
  • Addressed issue with Mapped Duplicate 3D time mapping inputs.
  • Addressed issue with selecting multiple titles clearing text.
  • Addressed issue with dropdown controls not always creating undo events.
  • Addressed issue with Follower animation using expressions.
  • Addressed issue with very small erode dilate levels.
  • Addressed issue with Film Look Creator gate weave controls.
  • Addressed issue with some scripts on ARM64 systems.
  • Addressed issue with slow reading of large EXR headers.
  • Addressed issue with OGraf custom text field sizes.
  • Support OGraf dropdown choice parameters.
  • Support OGraf rendering on Linux.
  • Improved OGraf inspector action controls.
  • General performance and stability improvements.
